summary:
**THE LAST WITNESS** is an immersive, interactive storytelling experience that brings the legacy of NASA's Mars exploration missions to life. Set on the Martian landscape of Jezero Crater, the project invites users to explore a cinematic 3D environment and uncover the story of humanity's robotic explorers, particularly NASA's Ingenuity Mars Helicopter.

Rather than presenting scientific information through conventional dashboards or static presentations, the experience uses environmental storytelling, interactive mission artifacts, and exploration-driven discovery to connect users emotionally with real space exploration achievements.

By combining Unreal Engine 5, 3D planetary visualization, and interactive elements, THE LAST WITNESS transforms mission history into an engaging digital experience. It highlights the scientific significance, technological ingenuity, and lasting legacy of robotic exploration while making NASA's discoveries more accessible, memorable, and meaningful to a wider audience.

Ultimately, it asks users to do more than learn about Mars: **to walk through its history and become a witness to the extraordinary machines that explored it.**
details:
What It Does & How It Works THE LAST WITNESS is an interactive narrative and mission telemetry archive chronicling the complete 72-flight journey of NASA’s Ingenuity Mars Helicopter across Jezero Crater. Structured into a multi-chapter expedition—from its 39.1-second maiden flight at Wright Brothers Field (Sol 58) through its aerial scouting campaigns to its final landing at Valinor Hills (Sol 1035)—the platform combines real NASA flight telemetry (altitude, groundspeed, rotor velocity, attitude, and coordinates) with interactive 3D visualizations, exploded rotorcraft schematics, and audio narration. Users can explore all 72 flights in a searchable logbook, inspect Mastcam-Z rotor blade damage findings, and experience Ingenuity’s ongoing "second life" as a stationary Martian weather and solar-flux monitor.

Benefits & Intended Impact Planetary exploration data is often locked inside dense scientific PDFs and raw Planetary Data System (PDS) tables. THE LAST WITNESS transforms raw mission logs into an emotionally resonant, accessible digital memorial and educational tool—bridging rigorous aerospace telemetry with human storytelling so students, educators, and the public can experience how an 1.8 kg technology demonstrator reshaped off-world aviation and paved the way for future Mars Sample Recovery helicopters and Dragonfly.

Tools, Languages & Software Used

  • Web Application & Frontend: HTML5, CSS3, JavaScript, Three.js / WebGL for interactive 3D flight dynamics and camera orbit controls, Web Audio API / speech synthesis for procedural soundscapes and voice narration, and structured JSON telemetry schemas.
  • 3D Terrain & Environment Prototyping: Unreal Engine 5 integrated with Cesium for Unreal to visualize Jezero Crater topography and landing sites.
  • Deployment & Version Control: GitHub and Vercel for continuous cloud hosting.
  • NASA Open Data: NASA JPL Ingenuity Mars Helicopter 72-Flight Log, Mars 2020 Mastcam-Z, HELI_RTE, and HELI_NAV raw image feeds, and NASA PDS4 localization archives.

Creativity & Design Considerations Rather than treating Ingenuity as a static museum entry, we framed the experience from the perspective of a "witness" left behind on another world—pairing live HUD telemetry readouts with atmospheric sound design and narrative pacing. Key design factors included historical and scientific fidelity to all 72 Sols, lightweight browser accessibility without requiring specialized hardware, and highlighting Ingenuity’s post-flight software update that allows it to continue logging Martian environmental data for future human explorers.
